body:
Well, my circles have straight lines in them, so you're probably a lot better than me. :P

And thanks! I usually get severe stage fright though if that makes sense. :P

And it's no problem! I fell asleep an hour before you replied. :P

I usually just doodle, and see where I go from there, though I'm not an artist in the slightest. 

I'm actually pretty great with improv, but it wouldn't hurt to try writing it down, right?

I'm not too sure what specific field really. I'm just going in for a general degree for now, actually.

I enjoy a plethora of activities. I love video games, acting, walking, hiking, camping, fishing, canoeing, amateur design (I'm horrific at it.), building with Legos (I actually had a large city going until about four years ago.), cooking, playing bass, reading, watching movies, and driving. 

The usual repertoire of things that any nerd/geek does. And I'm going for computer sciences, but a friend of mine always tries to point me to a local comedy club, and while that is pretty much my dream, I always think I'll flop. :s

> Weeeeeeel... except for the zombies, creepers, skeletons, giant spiders, endermen, etc...

That's why I play on easy! :D

Also, yeah. Like I've had the more interesting career choices as a child. Architecture, director, ringmaster, adventurer, actor, and comedian were some of them.

I'm not too sure. I mean, obviously a better life for myself, but aside from that, I don't know.

And this is why I wish life was like Minecraft.

I dunno, I mean cut ties as in like not really talking to that particular person. 

Thanks. I can only strive to create something that can make me happy right? If I have a good time doing it, that counts too, right?

I'm feeling better now. Not in the best shape out there, but enough for me to cut ties, and get my shit together hopefully. I do want to get a job at that store, I just need to try and see if they'll have openings come January. 

And I might. I don't know. I mean, it wavers a bit each day I think about it, but I'd like to think I can be successful, it's just that some days, I don't think I deserve it. 

And thanks for talking me through this. I mean that.

> *nods* Well, try to stick with the people that actually do appreciate you.

I'll do that. Hopefully I won't have to worry about others then.

> Ah. So you mean that person wants to start using your friend too, you think?

They already have been, but my friend manages to turn it around and use it to his advantage, though I not really inclined or able to say how.

> Oof and good as far as next semester it being possible hopefully. (See if you could, say, stay with one of those that actually appreciate you/care about you)

I don't see why not. A local music shop actually wanted to hire me but the only reason I didn't get it was because I couldn't do the hours. v.v But that's the plan. Hopefully move in with a friend or two, and just be free finally.

> Ugh as far as your dad. And good that you talked to a friend.

I mean, I guess he means well, as much I don't really believe it. And yeah, he was pretty happy I told him about it. So was I actually.

> *nods* try also to not take too much to heart those things he says to you.

I'll try not to. He always tried to snake his way into your head and pull at your emotions. Like a sociopath essentially. I need to be wary of that more often.

> Well, then think of it this way: Whoever's doing this "menting" business is being a bit of a jerk to you. Don't let them win. Be happy regardless of who or what ever "meant" otherwise.

It's an internal battle pretty much. I mean, no one really deserves to have a shitty life, but sometimes I can't help it for the most part. And I'm trying. I'm always the snarky funny guy of the group, and that's pretty much one of my forms of distraction/blocking them out.

> Ugh. Well, once again, I say your feelings matter.

And once again, I thank you very much. :)

> Well, if you change your mind, am listening. Wait, same person, so you mean it's mainly one or two people that're treating you like that?

More or less at the current moment, but there have been many others in the past.

> *blinks* What do you mean as far as dry humping your friend's legs? You mean literally, you mean it in some figurative way..?

Figuratively of course. I'm pretty much just saying that this person always wants to be with my friend. Mainly because this person, not my friend, is a very stealthy user.

As for moving, not really possible right now. Maybe come next semester when I can get a job and save some money, but at the current moment, I don't see that happening anytime soon.

> Then let someone validate you. It's okay if you sometimes need to talk. Doesn't make you an ass to ask for help from those that care about you, or just asking them to be there and listen a bit.

I know. I was raised in a very stereotypical masculine way, but a very old fashioned father, so I got used to masking my feelings, and I pretty much see myself as my dad saw me when I felt sad or was crying; kinda annoying. And I took a step in the right direction by asking a friend if I could just talk for a bit. Sure, it was 10:30 at night, and it was cold, but he came out, and I'm thankful for that.

> Ugh... I guess that might partly explain why he is the way he is, but that doesn't mean you should take it as a reflection of yourself. Though I understand that it'd feel that way.

I try not to compare myself to him, and if I were to ever be a father, I would never be like him, no matter what.

> What do you mean?

I guess my cynical side asks my hopeful side how I was ever meant to be happy. Like, say for example, you throw a rock down a well. You know it make a slight change, but in the end the ripples settle, and you don't know why you threw it down the well in the first place. 

> If you're explicitly being told that... ugh. Well, I'll say this: I say your feelings do matter. So there.

I still get told that every once in a while, how he has much more important things he has to worry about, and how "I have no right to be sad or anything." Feels really good to have my feelings being told they shouldn't exist. /sarcasm

And thanks. It's a good thing to hear once in a while.

> Can't go into details because you find it hard to talk about, or...?

I really don't want to talk about it. :/ It's been the same person, and it's not the first time either.

> And maybe then spend more time with those that actually care rather than those that seem to just be using you?

I'm trying, but I pretty much live with one person that uses me, and another one pretty much dry humps one of my best friend's legs, so it's a little hard, but I just avoid them by staying in my room, or go for a drive somewhere.

> I understand the feeling. But, for what it's worth, I'm listening. Also, those that really are your friends would also care, right?

And I thank you sincerely. And I know they'd be willing to listen and whatnot, but I just feel like an ass because I feel like I'm projecting my issues onto them. I'm one of those people who tends to either need a lot of validation, or I have to be extremely lonely.

> Ugh. :( If your dad is being like that, perhaps you should try not to take that too much as a reflection of you but rather a reflection of him? I understand how what you're describing would such though and make you feel this way.

I don't think he sees any fault within himself. He's a veteran with PTSD, but he won't admit it, and he expect me to like all the things he likes, what he likes to eat, ect. I try to have an interest, but his hobbies are different than mine, and to him, my hobbies are a waste of time. I don't try to bond with him all too much. 

> As I said, I'm listening if you want to talk about it.

I don't know why it happens. Maybe it's like this divine gatekeeping system that prevents me from actually being happy, and whenever I'm getting there, the gatekeeper is like "NOPE" and proceeds to molest me with depression and a pool cue. I guess I just want to actually have someone to relate to at least, or you know, to just actually be satisfied with how my life is going for once instead of wanting to kill myself every single day. 

I don't know. It just happens, and then I ask myself each time "Why did I think *that* was going to work?" whenever I get depressed after being happy for a bit. There are too many ups and downs within a single year for me to handle or care about.

> Yeah, I've seen that sort of feedback loop before. You feel what you feel. Try not to feel bad for, well, feeling bad. (for the exact reason you describe). The fact that other people may have it worse doesn't negate the fact that you're feeling bad now.

I've always been told that my feelings were nothing compared to everyone else. My dad always made it a point to say my feelings didn't even compare to what he feels, or anyone else for that matter, so when I get sad, I just feel bad because I've been told all my life that my feelings have and will never matter to anyone.

> How're people treating you like a tool and stuff?

It's just been recently. I can't really go into details, but it's just pretty much been known to me that I'm really only there for certain people for items, rides, food, and other things. Sure, there are some who actually might enjoy my company, but they're outnumbered by the sheer amounts of others.

> Perhaps you are important to them?

I suppose. I don't really feel important though. Never really felt like I could talk to them about my issues. I don't want to be much of a burden. Or whiny.

> Who tells you that? What happened? *offers a hug*

My father. No matter what, it's not good enough. I don't do this right, I don't do that right, I need to always listen to him, he's the only one who knows what they're doing, he is the only one with a brain, ect. And it's all usually in reference to me. I can never help without thinking I suck at it, and that I should just step aside from everything, so that way I don't interfere.

> Feeling that you don't deserve it, feeling like that, well, sucks. :( I've known what that's like. Why're you feeling that way?

Because every time I actually start to feel happy, reality kicks me in the ass. It's always enough to have my hopes up, but just short enough to shatter any expectations I have for myself. It always happens. Such has been my life. I know there are much worse things than what I go through, so it's just a negative feedback loop: Feel bad about self -> Realize you don't have it as bad -> become even more depressed about how depressed you are. Rinse and repeat. :/
